newsitem.title: USA: Oil refinery fire put out in Los Angeles suburb.
newsitem.headline: Oil refinery fire put out in Los Angeles suburb.

text.p: A thunderous explosion ripped through a Texaco oil refinery on Monday, causing an intense fire that sent columns of smoke and flame into the sky.
There were no reports of deaths or injuries as more than 150 firefighters battled the blaze in the Los Angeles suburb of Wilmington, officials said.
A spokesman for the Los Angeles city fire department said the firefighters extinguished the morning blaze in just over an hour.
"The cause is still under investigation," spokesman Brian Humphrey said.

The explosion was so powerful it was heard miles away, and news helicopters hovering overhead showed blackened, twisted metal wreckage in one section of the refinery. Clouds of black smoke billowed hundreds of feet into the air.
Fire officials said the explosion occurred in a hydrotreater, where sulfur compounds are separated from crude oil in the production process. The fire was also limited to that section.

The fire raged out out of control at first, but firefighters quickly gained the upper hand. "It's not contained but it's confined," a fire department spokesman told reporters. "The fire's not going anyplace else."

The spokesman said arson investigators were called to the scene as a routine measure but the cause of the explosion was still under investigation. The extent of the damage was not known, and it was expected to be hours before it would be safe for firefighters to inspect the structure.
Dozens of workers were evacuated from the plant, and streets in the area were closed to normal traffic. "No employees were injured, and everyone's been accounted for," the spokesman said.
Residents said they felt the ground shake and at first thought there had been an earthquake.
Humphrey earlier called the fire "a very, very dangerous" one to fight and said refineries throughout the area had sent their personnel to help.
The Texaco refinery takes in 64,000 barrels a day of crude oil, turning it into a variety of refined products, including gasoline.
